title: Move `forces` into its own document in database

comments_data.body: I'm still working on this PR

Thanks for this @lilitkarapetyan - it looks good.  I have one question: will it work with a _legacy_ SQLite database, where the data is _all_ in the `wargame` document?   For the wargame that ran this week, I may still need to be able open/show the game state in Serge.
Hello Ian, no it won't work with the old SQLite database, but can I make it work with the old database as well

> Hello Ian, no it won't work with the old SQLite database, but can I make it work with the old database as well

Here is the challenge @lilitkarapetyan :
* from the game last week we have a large body of test data.  It uses the current "model" of having a really large `wargame` document
* the clients and I would like to run more tests against this data, including testing how adjudication should work.  So, I'll be running new versions of `Serge` software against that database file

So, I can think of these options:
1. update their SQLite database to separate out the two documents, then use updated Serge. Aah, there are actually several versions of the wargame document - and I've have to update all of them.
2. keep this PR open until we/they have finished testing the data (about 2 months, I guess). But, no-one likes a PR sitting around.
3. make this PR support their database format, but "retire" this legacy support when they have finished testing. Note: this isn't all that difficult.  The database will _either_ be in the new format or the old format.  So, `newState` will either receive an object with all the data, or it will receive just the `wargame`, plus a separate document of `settings`, which it will put into `newState`.

What do you think @lilitkarapetyan  - do you have a favourite option?

Do you have a preferred option?
I think the second version will be good because we will have more time to study and check the data, this is an important change
of the other two options, I would prefer the first
So, option 2 (`keep this PR open`) is your favourite solution @lilitkarapetyan ?
Well,  it's not my favorite, but I think it's the best solution in this case because we're going to make an important change to our project.
we can also do with the first option
Hello @IanMayo, can you check this PR ?

Hello @lilitkarapetyan - These are a set steps to force wargame changes.  They cause new versions of the `Forces` document to be created.  The updates appear to be working properly.

1. run `yarn develop`
2. login as game control: http://localhost:3000/?wargame=wargame-l6nngxlk&access=umpire
3. open `Adjudications` tab
4. click on `Get next`, a new `Interaction` will be created (this is a new document in SQLite, too)
5. make panel wide enough to see form, and scroll down the form to the `Health outcomes`
6. modify the health of `Red:22` to `0`
7. move back up to the `Perception Outcomes`
8. add a new row
9. select Asset `Red:22`, provide `dolphin` as the `Name`
10. scroll down to bottom, click on `Submit Adjudication`
11. switch to `Orders` tab
12. type `Red:22` into search box, `Red:22` should be at the top of the listing
13. it does now who a health of `0`

Aah, the GameAdmin pages don't work, since they still expect to find a `Forces` object the `wargame` object in `RootState`.  
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/218117444-3812bb99-2366-41bf-b03c-02d9a2d3c9d1.png)


I guess we need to either change RootState (to put in the ForceData[] array, or need to put the `ForceData[]` array into the `wargame` object for `RootState`.  The first one seems like better engineering.
Closing this PR.  It's no longer relevant after our switch to `core-mapping`
